report:
## Summary
Marta's acquisition of the "Lena" target has been fast and largely errorless: the recallable interval climbed from 15s to the full 960s ceiling within five daily sessions. There is one clear sign of between-session softening — a missed start-of-day probe on session 4 — but the pattern overall does not show a repeated or worsening decay trend; it recovered the very next day.

## Acquisition trajectory
Recall was established quickly. Session 1 (2026‑07‑03) had 7/7 trials correct, peaking at a 33.75s interval. Session 2 (07‑04) climbed to 75.94s despite one miss (5/6 correct). Session 3 (07‑05) jumped sharply to 576.65s with a clean 7/7 sheet — the biggest single-session gain in the series. Session 4 (07‑06) reached 864.98s (2/3 correct, one miss), and session 5 (07‑07) reached the configured ceiling of 960s with 3/3 correct. In five practice days, Marta went from a 15‑second starting interval to the maximum interval the protocol allows, which is a rapid acquisition rate for this one fact.

## Reset & recovery behavior
Two in-session misses occurred (session 2 and session 4), plus one missed start-of-day probe (session 4). In each case the ladder behaved as expected: the miss was corrected on the spot, and the *next* successful climb still reached a new high-water mark rather than stalling — session 2's max (75.94s) exceeded session 1's, and session 4's max (864.98s) exceeded session 3's. This is consistent with the intended expanding-ladder design: a miss drops the interval back and triggers immediate correction, but does not erase the overall upward trend within the same practice arc. There is no case in this log where a miss was followed by a lower session ceiling than the one before it.

## Interval band reached
Marta reliably reached the configuration ceiling of 960 seconds on session 5, with a clean 3/3 trial sheet. Sessions 3 and 4 already sat close to that ceiling (576.65s and 864.98s respectively), so the climb from "in progress" to "at ceiling" took only two more sessions. Within-session ladder work for this target now appears complete in the sense that there is no higher interval left to climb to under the current ceiling — the open question going forward is start-of-day consistency, not further interval expansion.

## Schedule & booster state
The target is on a "between-session" schedule with a 1‑day gap (consistent with the configured firstGap), next due 2026‑07‑08. Booster step is still 0 — Marta has not yet advanced into the booster cadence (7/14/30/90 days), which only begins after mastery. The mastery counter (start‑streak) currently sits at 1: sessions 1–3 opened with clean recall, session 4's start probe was missed (streak reset, corrected), and session 5's start probe was recalled again, restarting the count toward the needed streak of 3 clean start-of-day recalls. Target 1 is marked "mastered: false," with 0 bad sessions logged.

## Limitations (n=1)
This is a single dyad's practice log for one target ("Lena"), not a controlled study. It can responsibly inform *this* patient's own protocol tuning — for instance, whether the interval ceiling or gap needs adjusting for her — but it cannot answer or settle any general question about spaced retrieval as a method: not whether expanding intervals outperform uniform ones, not whether errorless practice outperforms effortful retrieval, and not what "typical" acquisition or decay rates look like across patients or etiologies. There is no control condition, no comparison target or comparison person, and no way to separate the effect of the schedule itself from other factors (time of day, mood, environment, practice mode) that could have influenced any single session's outcome. The one missed start-probe (session 4) is a single data point — not enough to characterize a decay trend, only enough to note that it happened once and resolved by the next session.
